newsitem.title: USA: Ford shakes up senior management.
newsitem.headline: Ford shakes up senior management.

text.p: Ford Motor Co announced a senior management shakeup on Thursday, naming group vice president Jacques Nasser to replace Edward Hagenlocker as president of Ford Automotive Operations.
Hagenlocker was named a vice chairman, overseeing a new organization that includes automotive components, land development, technical affairs and rental car operations.
Also named a vice chairman was executive vice president Wayne Booker, who was is in charge of the automaker's international operations.
Chief Financial Officer and Group Vice President John Devine was promoted to executive vice president, keeping his current duties.
Ford said it promoted Vice President James Englehart to take Nasser's old job of group vice president responsible for product development.

The moves, which had been rumored for months, intensify the race to succeed Alex Trotman, who currently holds the chairman, chief executive and president titles. In 1998, Trotman reaches the mandatory retirement age of 65, but the board could ask him to stay on longer.
In a statement, Trotman said the moves will help the company streamline its component operations into a single enterprise that will be more competitive.

"We are separating the automotive components business from Ford Automotive Operations to focus senior management attention on making it more competitive in its own right," he said. "I have asked Ed Hagenlocker to take on the crucial assignment of making this happen."
